transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-14
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Mark Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Luis Gomez (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (NovaCredit CTO), Maya Singh (Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Infra Lead), Sara Park (Security)

Summary: quick discovery focused on Dedicated reserved GPU needs, isolation/VPC requirements, burst strategy, and scaling expectations. Customer wants predictable throughput for credit risk scoring model and needs details on isolation, KMS, and pilot timeline.

Topics: dedicated capacity sizing, reserved vs burst, private deployment/VPC, KMS/encryption, onboarding timeline, success criteria, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Mark (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Valentine's day. I'm Mark from Redwood, AE on this account. We also have Priya and Luis from our SE team. Could folks introduce themselves quickly?
[00:10] Alex (NovaCredit): Sure hi, Alex here, CTO, Maya leads ML, Tom infra, Sara handles security, thanks for setting this up.
[00:18] Mark: Great, goal for today is to understand your workloads, whether you're leaning hosted, dedicated, or private, but sounds like dedicated is top of mind?
[00:27] Maya: Yeah, primarily dedicated. We run a credit risk model that serves low-latency scoring for loan decisions, about 150 qps peak, offline batch and online. We need isolation and predictable throughput.
[00:40] Priya (Redwood SE): Got it. Can you give rough model size and token characteristics? Are you using a T5-like encoder-decoder or a causal large model?
[00:49] Maya: It's a fine-tuned Llama2-70B variant — mostly shorter sequences, 128 tokens typical, some long tail 512. Latency target 200-300ms p95 for single request scoring.
[01:02] Tom (Infra): And from infra we need VPC peering or private link, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also need to know the isolation levels — are GPUs multi-tenant or fully reserved for the customer?
[01:15] Luis (Redwood SE): For Dedicated we provision a reserved GPU pool per account; that gives you dedicated compute nodes not shared with other tenants. You can also set burst policies to use spare capacity from a shared pool for short bursts, but customer data stays isolated at storage and network layers.
[01:30] Sara (Security): How does KMS integration work? We need envelope encryption with our keys and HSM compatibility. SOC2 and ISO attestations obviously required.
[01:38] Priya: We support customer-managed KMS via our Private deployments and dedicated integrations for Dedicated — we can do CMEK with GCP/Azure/AWS KMS and HSM-backed keys; we'll share the integration docs. We also have SOC 2 Type II and ISO certs — will attach those.
[01:52] Alex: Cool. For performance, what's the recommended GPU shape and how do you size for 150 qps at our model?
[01:59] Priya: With Llama2-70B and 128 tokens typical, a conservative starting point is a pool of 4 A100-80GB equivalents with the optimized kernels and continuous batching — that gives headroom. If your tail has 512 tokens and you need tighter p95, we'd recommend 6-8 GPUs. We can run a benchmark to precise the sizing.
[02:15] Mark: Pricing aside, the big tradeoff is cost vs latency. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, hosted is cheaper for variable workloads but multi-tenant. Do you expect sustained baseline traffic or big sporadic bursts?
[02:27] Maya: Baseline is 60-80 qps, spikes to ~150 during morning hours and sometimes when marketing batch runs. Spikes last 20-40 minutes.
[02:36] Tom: We need autoscaling behavior — if the reserved pool is saturated, can Redwood burst to capacity in another region or a shared pool? And what's the failover behavior?
[02:45] Luis: Yes, you can configure burst to a shared pool or to alternate capacity tiers; policies define max burst and fallback model variants. For strict SLAs we recommend reserved plus a small burst buffer. Failover: requests can route to a compatible quantized variant with slightly higher latency but preserved availability.
[03:02] Alex: So for our SLA we want guaranteed p95 under baseline and graceful degradation for spikes. Can you guarantee that in contract?
[03:09] Mark: We offer SLA-backed latency targets on Dedicated with committed capacity. We can put a latency SLO into the contract tied to the reserved GPU count; that is part of the Dedicated enterprise plan.
[03:18] Sara: Regarding data residency, logs should stay in our VPC and not be forwarded to Redwood's shared storage. Is private deployment required for that?
[03:27] Priya: You have two options. Dedicated with VPC peering keeps network traffic within your VPC and we provide per-tenant audit logs that can be forwarded to your SIEM. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for stricter control where the control plane is isolated. We'll map controls to your compliance needs.
[03:42] Tom: If we go with Dedicated reserved GPUs, what's the onboarding timeline? We want pilot in 4 weeks, full production in 8-10 weeks if pilot goes well.
[03:50] Mark: Typical pilot timeline for Dedicated is 2-4 weeks for a canary: sizing, provisioning a small reserved pool, run benchmarks, iterate. Full production depending on procurement and network setup can be 6-10 weeks. Your 4 week pilot is reasonable.
[04:03] Maya: For the pilot we want cost estimates for a 4-GPU and a 6-GPU pool, and an option with a 4-GPU reserved + 2-GPU burst. Also, what's the billing model for reserved vs burst?
[04:13] Mark: Reserved is monthly committed pricing; burst is metered on usage. We'll send a pricing sheet with both committed and burst economics.
[04:20] Alex: On the technical side, we need details about kv cache behavior and warm starts — our requests are independent but would benefit from prefix caching for similar prompts.
[04:28] Priya: We support KV caching and prefix reuse; for scoring workloads where contexts repeat, that reduces per-token latency and cost. We'll capture your prompt patterns in the benchmark plan.
[04:35] Sara: One more security question: can you rotate keys without downtime? And are audit logs tamper-evident?
[04:42] Luis: Key rotation supported with minimal disruption via envelope keys and a key versioning scheme; audit logs are tamper-evident when forwarded to your SIEM with our signed log hooks. We'll include the security runbook.
[04:53] Maya: Who owns AMI/container images? We prefer bringing our own container with the model.
[04:58] Priya: You can bring your own container and model artifacts; Dedicated supports customer-owned images and model artifacts, subject to validation. For on-prem/Private we support fully air-gapped deployments.
[05:06] Tom: If we want burst into another region for disaster scenarios, how do you handle cross-region latency and data residency?
[05:14] Luis: Cross-region bursting is possible but data residency constraints may apply; you can limit burst targets to regions that meet your residency. Latency will increase, so for DR we recommend cold standby in the same region or a nearby region with acceptable latency.
[05:26] Mark: Quick recap: NovaCredit baseline 60-80 qps, peaks ~150 qps, model Llama2-70B fine-tuned, target p95 200-300ms, want reserved Dedicated with burst buffer and VPC peering, CMEK/KMS integration, SOC2/ISO docs, pilot in ~4 weeks. Next steps are to send pricing and security docs, plan benchmark.
[05:44] Alex: Sounds good. We'd also like a written runbook for incident response and rollback for model regressions.
[05:50] Priya: We'll include an ops runbook and propose a canary rollout strategy (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic fallback to previous model if quality drops.
[05:59] Maya: Can you also include quantization recommendations? We care about cost but don't want quality regressions.
[06:05] Luis: We'll include quantization and kernel/compilation profiles; for Llama2-70B we can test 4-bit quantization options, measure quality delta on your eval set.
[06:13] Tom: Procurement question — do you offer annual committed discounts and how firm is the reserved capacity price?
[06:19] Mark: Yes annual commitments get deeper discounts and we can offer a multi-year rate lock for Dedicated. We'll include both monthly and annual options.
[06:26] Sara: Please include the contact for security SOC2 attestation and any pen test reports.
[06:31] Mark: Will do.
[06:34] Alex: Ok let's wrap, thanks.
[06:36] Mark: Thanks all. We'll send the pricing, security pack, and a proposed benchmark plan. Priya will run the benchmark and follow up to schedule the pilot.
[06:45] End of recording.
